title: Generic etaleness of the concrete strict-hensel root normalization
statement:
Let $i:U	o L$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $G$ a finite group and $W	o U$ a finite etale $G$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Let $R$ be a commutative regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], $\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}R	o L$, and $f\in R$ a nonzerodivisor with $R/(f)$ regular. Suppose $|G|$ is a unit in $R$. Assume $ eta:U	imes_L\operatorname{Spec}R\cong D(f)$ commutes with the projection to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $ ar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega	o\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], $H$ its canonical strict henselization coordinate-ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and $b:R	o H$ a map inducing its structural morphism [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Put $g=b(f)$, $n_0=|G|$, $A=H[T]/(T^{n_0}-g)$, $N=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $q:N	o\operatorname{Spec}H$ the algebra structural morphism, and $V=D(g)\subset N$. Assume $g$ is not a unit. Suppose $N$ is locally Noetherian. Let $p:W	imes_L V	o V$ be the second pullback projection along $V\hookrightarrow N\xrightarrow{q}\operatorname{Spec}H\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}b}\operatorname{Spec}R\xrightarrow{\varphi}L$, and assume $p$ is finite and etale [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Put $a=p\circ(V\hookrightarrow N)$ and let $a^
u:C_a	o N$ be its concrete relative normalization [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization], defined affine locally by integral closure in the sections of the source of $a$. Assume $a^
u$ is finite. Fix a regular integral scheme $D$ and an effective Cartier centre $j:D	o N$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] such that every $z\in N$ lies in $V$ exactly when it lies outside $j(D)$. Let $\eta\in D$ be a generic point of $D$. Then there exists an open $O\subseteq N$ containing $j(\eta)$ such that $a^
u$ restricted to $O$ is etale. No construction or finiteness of a new model, and no identification over $V$, is asserted.

proof.text: First transport the retained upstream regular-divisor quotient theorem from the full affine-neighbourhood colimit to H through smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso. The theorem smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso_toBase identifies the structural maps. Pull the nonunit condition back through the inverse ring equivalence. Transfer Noetherianity by isNoetherianRing_of_ringEquiv and the quotient properties by Ideal.quotientEquiv, IsRegularRing.of_ringEquiv and MulEquiv.isDomain_iff. The strict henselization regular-divisor quotient gives Noetherianness and a regular domain quotient. Apply the existing affine-chart ind-etaleness theorem with the identity chart of Spec R and the identity isomorphism of the small strict-henselization scheme. The hypothesis on b is exactly its structure-map compatibility. Forget the resulting filtered etale algebra presentation to modules; etale stages are flat, and the same-universe flat-colimit-presentation theorem gives flatness of b. Flat base change preserves regularity of f. The root-algebra theorem then gives regular local rings at primes containing the root coordinate.

Apply the generic source-etaleness theorem to the concrete root normalization. It gives a source open neighbourhood of each normalization point over j(eta), with the exact finite-fibre hypotheses of the target.

Finiteness of the morphism lets source-local etaleness over the finite fibre be shrunk to a target open neighbourhood by the finite-source Zariski-locality argument. This yields the required O containing j(eta).

lean.statement:
theorem GaloisCover.strict_hensel_root_normalization_generic_etale
    {L U : Scheme.{u}} (i : U ⟶ L)
    (G : Type (u + 1)) [Group G] [Finite G] (W : GaloisCover G U)
    (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (φ : Spec R ⟶ L) (f : R)
    (hG : IsUnit (Nat.card G : R))
    [IsRegularRing R] (hf : IsSMulRegular R f)
    [IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f})]
    (β : pullback i φ ≅ Scheme.Opens.toScheme (X := Spec R) (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f))
    (hβ : β.hom ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (X := Spec R) (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f) = pullback.snd i φ)
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (barY : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec R)
    (b : R ⟶ strictHenselizationRing barY)
    (hb : Spec.map b = strictHenselizationStructuralMap barY) :
    let H := strictHenselizationRing barY
    let g := b.hom f
    let A := AdjoinRoot ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial H) ^ Nat.card G - Polynomial.C g)
    let N := Spec (CommRingCat.of A)
    let q := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap H A))
    let V : N.Opens := PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (algebraMap H A g)
    ¬ IsUnit g → ∀ (hN : IsLocallyNoetherian N),
    letI := hN
    let p := pullback.snd (W.π ≫ i) (V.ι ≫ q ≫ Spec.map b ≫ φ)
    ∀ (hp : IsFinite p),
    letI := hp
    let a := p ≫ V.ι
    Etale p → IsFinite a.fromNormalization →
    ∀ (D : Scheme.{u}) (j : D ⟶ N),
      IsRegular D → IsIntegral D → IsEffectiveCartierCenter j →
      (∀ z : N, z ∈ V ↔ z ∉ Set.range j) →
      ∀ (η : D), IsGenericPoint η Set.univ →
      ∃ (O : N.Opens), j η ∈ O ∧ Etale (a.fromNormalization ∣_ O)
